clue.text: Careful poet has no right to a set of books

indicators.note: the poet is said to lack something, so a letter is dropped from his name

parts.note: Virgil is the Roman poet of the Aeneid
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A cautious poet is denied the right to own a collection of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes R out of VIRGIL, leaving VIGIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vigilant is watchful and on guard, which is to say careful.

clue.text: Cloth-worker's residence in Wakefield?

parts.note: a man of the cloth is a clergyman, and Goldsmith's novel features one from Wakefield, so his home is meant, not a textile worker's

explanation.surface: Where a textile worker lives in the Yorkshire town of Wakefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloth-worker' suggests the Yorkshire wool trade; it is a man of the cloth, as in Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's official house in his parish is his manse or rectory, here the one for the Wakefield churchman.

clue.text: Variety of pear given by this plant? Certainly not

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Does this plant produce a kind of pear? Of course not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges PEAR and GIVEN together; the closing 'Certainly not' jokes that this plant gives grapes, not pears.
explanation.definitionFit: The vine that bears grapes is a climbing plant.

clue.text: A 28 can be put up for this tropical plant

indicators.note: in a down entry put up means written upwards, so the pieces read bottom to top

parts.note: 28 across is a claw, and a nail is another word for a claw

explanation.surface: A hook could be raised to hang this jungle plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 across means claw; A NAIL turned upward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical rainforests.

clue.text: A sign originally lit up in New York in an objectionable way

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the city's abbreviation
originally means at the beginning, taking the first letter of sign
in a down entry up means the word lit is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lit taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A sign first lit up in New York looked offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letter of sign, and 'up' reads lit backwards in this down entry; the run then sits inside New York's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastily means unpleasantly or offensively, in a disagreeable manner.

clue.text: Panic about carbon being in short supply

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a scare is a panic or sudden fright
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads because carbon has become hard to get.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce goods are rare, scanty, hard to come by.

clue.text: Island cereal is fit for a goat!

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Grain from an island makes good goat feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is the zodiac sign represented by a goat.

clue.text: Sounds like foul sleeping accommodation!

parts.note: foul is said the same as fowl, so the clue asks for the place where birds sleep, not a dirty bed

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the bedroom is filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' suggests dirty lodgings; said aloud it is fowl, as in poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickens and other birds settle at night on a perch or shelter where they sleep.

clue.text: The, team in the Spanish uniform

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine word for the
even means uniform, regular, level

explanation.surface: The side takes the field in Spain's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'The' only links; 'uniform' is an adjective, not a kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has that many players, so the word names a team.

clue.text: Once-presumptuous virtuoso

parts.note: ex means former, once
pert means cheeky or presumptuous

explanation.surface: A virtuoso who used to be arrogant.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a person of outstanding skill, a master of an art.

clue.text: Start to court the French artist's girl

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, taken from the word court

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A young woman connected with a French painter begins to be wooed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a woman's given name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Instrument unknown in Poona? He's mistaken

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: x is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity
the letters of he's taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims an instrument is unheard of in the Indian city of Poona, but is told he's wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges X, POONA and HES together.
explanation.definitionFit: The saxophone is a reed instrument of the woodwind family.

clue.text: Question further about former partner having an explosive device

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
an ex is a former husband, wife or partner
an means a single one, giving the letter A
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: Questioning a former spouse again after an ex turns up carrying a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something again or interrogate a witness a second time is to question further.

clue.text: Fibre featured in a Whistler painting

indicators.note: featured in says the letters appear within the words a Whistler painting

explanation.surface: Some textile fibre appears in a canvas by the American painter Whistler.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a plant fibre from agave or yucca, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Deny it's fashionable in Georgia, for example

indicators.note: in places the fashionable word inside the state's abbreviation plus the example word

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
say is used to introduce an example
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: Someone denies that something is in vogue in Georgia, giving an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or refuse to admit, a formal word for deny.

clue.text: Amazed that a Caribbean island is insured?

definitions.text: Amazed that a Caribbean island is insured?

parts.words: Amazed that a Caribbean island is insured?
parts.note: read insured as in sured: PR for Puerto Rico and IS sit inside the made-up word sured, giving a word for astonished

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that a Caribbean island has an insurance policy.
explanation.walkthrough: PR (Puerto Rico) plus IS go 'in SURED'; since SURED is no real word the clue is a cryptic definition rather than a clean container.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken aback by something unexpected is being astonished.

clue.text: Hard worker taking in, and taken in by,'a 24?

definitions.text: taking in, and taken in by,'a 24?

explanation.surface: A diligent worker both admits and is fooled by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is HORSE: the people of Troy took the wooden horse into their city and were taken in by its trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is to toil hard; and the citizens of ancient Troy both admitted the wooden horse and were deceived by it.

clue.text: George gives gold to a sanctimonious crew

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
pi is short for pious, meaning sanctimonious
a lot is a group or crew of people

explanation.surface: A man named George hands gold to a self-righteous team.
explanation.walkthrough: George is RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight control George, so the slang name means the self-steering system.

clue.text: Antagonize holy man found in Eastern mountains

indicators.note: found in puts the holy man inside the other pieces

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains
St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A holy man in the eastern hills makes enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate or turn someone hostile.

clue.text: Unintentionally reveal girl's rendez-vous with boy

parts.note: Bet is a short form of the girl's name Elizabeth
Ray is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young woman's secret meeting with a lad is accidentally given away.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray a feeling is to let it show without meaning to, giving it away.

clue.text: After study, the route up appeared wide-open

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the pieces are read from the bottom
after puts the route word behind the study word before turning

parts.note: a den is a private study
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Following study, the uphill road looked wide open.
explanation.walkthrough: DEN then WAY, read upwards as one, gives YAW + NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening the mouth wide in tiredness, or a chasm gaping, both look like this.

clue.text: Summary of meeting taking 61 seconds?

explanation.surface: Writing up the notes of a meeting takes just over a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 61 seconds is more than one minute, so the time taken is literally plural minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: The written record of a meeting is called its minutes; and sixty-one seconds is a little more than one minute, so a span of more than one.

clue.text: Mountaineers' leader unusually docile? It's to do with the air

definitions.text: It's to do with the air

indicators.note: the leader of mountaineers is the first letter of that word
unusually means in an odd manner, so the letters of docile are shuffled

explanation.surface: The head climber is oddly meek; perhaps it's the thin air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the air' is a tune, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic means relating to melody, and an air is a tune.

clue.text: A counterstroke

parts.note: split as counter plus stroke: a sideboard serving food, and a blow

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'counterstroke' into counter (a self-service food table) and stroke (a blow, as in buffeted by the wind).
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a counter where food is served, and to buffet is to strike, so both halves fit.

clue.text: In the Soviet Union he replaces second son as guide

indicators.note: replaces says the word he takes the place of the second son's letter

parts.note: USSR stands for the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
he taken as written

explanation.surface: In the USSR a man takes the place of a second son as a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second son' points at the second S of USSR (S = son); swapping it for HE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats in a theatre or church, acting as a guide.

clue.text: Husky — not a beast of burden

indicators.note: not says the letter is to be left out

parts.note: a husky voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: A husky dog is no pack animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the sled dog but means rough-voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is used for carrying loads and pulling carts, a draught animal.

clue.text: Fats coating 'invalid food for decoration

indicators.note: coating means wrapping round, so one name goes outside the food

parts.note: Fats Waller was a famous American jazz pianist
pap is soft mushy food for invalids or babies

explanation.surface: Fatty coatings on invalid food serve as decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fats' looks like grease but is the jazz pianist Fats Waller.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallpaper is printed paper pasted on walls as interior decoration.

clue.text: Climbing peak to find the kinkajou

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the word reads upwards

parts.note: top means peak

explanation.surface: Ascending a summit to spot a tropical animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns TOP upwards to POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Potto is an old name also applied to the kinkajou, a tree-dwelling mammal of tropical America.

clue.text: Where ploughmen are fated, possibly, to carry weapons

indicators.note: to carry means to hold, so the shuffled word goes around the weapons
possibly suggests the letters of fated could be arranged another way

parts.note: arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Doomed ploughmen are perhaps fated to bear arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles fated, and 'to carry' wraps those shuffled letters around the weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmstead is a farm with its buildings, the home base of farm workers such as ploughmen.

clue.text: Claw the cards

explanation.surface: Grab the playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a bird of prey's claw; in card games the talon is the stock of cards left after dealing.

clue.text: These clothes are affectedly dainty and extremely decorous

parts.note: twee means quaint or affectedly dainty

indicators.note: the extremes of decorous are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: These garments are fussily pretty and very proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeds are suits or outfits made of the rough woollen cloth tweed.

clue.text: A cricket club with eccentric attire

parts.note: outre means unconventional or eccentric

explanation.surface: A cricket club turns out in strange clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to equip or dress someone, so to attire them.
